content:
Let \(p\) be the number of planet cards currently held. A hegemon card is worth \(4p\), while a planet card is worth \(2010\).

So a planet card is chosen while
\[
4p < 2010 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p \le 502.
\]
Starting with \(p=0\), on turn \(n\) we have \(p=n-1\) as long as we take planets. Thus we take planets for
\[
n-1 \le 502 \implies n \le 503.
\]
So \(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{503}=0\), and after turn \(503\) we have \(p=503\).

From turn \(504\) onward,
\[
4p = 4(503)=2012 > 2010,
\]
so a hegemon card is always worth more. Therefore \(a_n=1\) for all \(n\ge 504\), which is periodic with period \(1\). The tail starting at \(503\) is \(0,1,1,1,\ldots\), which is not periodic.

Thus the smallest such \(N\) is
\[
\boxed{504}.
\]
